newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan to sell off more big enterprises.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan to sell off more big enterprises.

text.p: Turkmenistan is launching the second stage of its privatisation programme, in line with a law adopted earlier this month by the parliament, a government official said on Thursday.

An official from the economy and finance ministry told Reuters that in line with the law -- adopted on June 12 and now coming into force -- the Turkmen government would soon hold tenders for 100 large industrial enterprises.
He said Turkmen citizens and non-residents would be allowed to take part in the tenders for the companies, which include a glass works and a cement factory.
The Central Asian state will set up a special body to supervise the tenders, and all the proceeds from the sell-offs will be channelled to the state budget, the official said.

In line with "1,000 days" -- an ambitious economic programme presented by strongman President Saparmurat Niyazov in April -- Turkmenistan will pass into private hands 330 out of 375 industrial enterprises by the year 2000.
But 45 companies -- representing oil and gas industries, railways, pipelines and civil aviation, are exempt from Turkmenistan's privatisation programme.
Officials say mass privatisation was carried out in Turkmenistan last year, as hundreds of services, trade and public catering companies passed into private hands.
But there is little independent evidence of how many Turkmens became real private owners in the resource-rich but impoverished state.
